content.value_statement: Unclear requirements lead to oversized projects and costly technology choices. This skill turns requirements and research into an approved scope, priorities, estimates, and stack decision.
actual_capabilities: Collects project requirements and clarifies only decision-relevant gaps.
Loads existing RESEARCH documents when available.
Prioritizes features with Must, Should, Could, and Won't categories.
Estimates relative feature size with T-shirt sizing.
Presents stack options and requests approval before confirming them.
limitations: It does not write application code or create a project scaffold.
It does not perform broad market or technical research by itself.
Estimates are relative planning signals, not delivery commitments.
Stack recommendations need user approval and may need specialist review.

use_cases.title: Plan an MVP
use_cases.description: Turn an early product idea into a small, prioritized feature set and a documented MVP boundary.

use_cases.title: Align a delivery team
use_cases.description: Create a shared scope document before developers begin architecture or scaffolding work.

use_cases.title: Review a client brief
use_cases.description: Clarify requirements, exclusions, estimates, and technology constraints before preparing a delivery proposal.

prompt_templates.title: Start a simple scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /scope for a habit-tracking mobile app for students. Keep the first release small.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a feature list
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /scope for an internal support portal. Separate Must, Should, Could, and Won't features.

prompt_templates.title: Use research input
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /scope --from docs/research/RESEARCH-support-portal.md for a support portal MVP. Compare stack options and ask for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a planning brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /scope --quick for a multilingual appointment-booking service. Identify XL risks, exclusions, and the smallest viable stack.

output_examples.input: Scope a habit-tracking app for students.
output: Must: create habits, mark daily completion, view streaks.
Won't now: social sharing, wearable integration, and advanced analytics.
Estimated scope: three Must features, sized S to M.

output_examples.input: Compare stack options for an MVP booking service.
output: Recommendation: select a managed backend that supports authentication and scheduling.
Reason: it meets the Must features with lower operational effort.
Next step: request user approval before recording the final stack.

best_practices: Provide the target user, core problem, and delivery constraints before starting.
Use existing research documents as evidence for stack decisions.
Review Must features carefully and approve the stack before scaffolding.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every requested feature as a Must feature.
Do not use relative estimates as fixed delivery promises.
Do not confirm a costly stack decision without user approval.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It produces scope and stack decisions before implementation begins.

faq.question: What is MoSCoW prioritization?
faq.answer: It groups features into Must, Should, Could, and Won't categories.

faq.question: Can I skip technology-stack selection?
faq.answer: Yes. Use --skip-stack when you only need a scope decision.

faq.question: Can I use existing research?
faq.answer: Yes. Use --from with a RESEARCH document, or let the skill look in docs/research.

faq.question: Does it overwrite earlier scope documents?
faq.answer: No. It uses date-based names to keep existing SCOPE documents.

faq.question: When should I use --stdout?
faq.answer: Use --stdout when you want the scope in the conversation without creating a file.
